The blood fill cue borrows from design-coded bullet lists and the modern blood-type-marker aesthetic, which is exactly why the emoji reads as blood coded rather than literal b-button-coded shape.

In real-world usage 🅱️ lives in the spaces where the sender wants to communicate blood-type-marker energy. A partner sends it on a 'blood 🅱️' blood-type-marker marker. A friend sends it on a 'b-pulse pulse 🅱️' reveal. A coworker sends it on a 'blood coded 🅱️' list thread. The blood fill cue is what makes the emoji feel blood coded — it is not just 'shape,' it is 'blood coded b-button moment.'

What separates 🅱️ from the rest of the shape family is the blood register. The emoji is not saying 'solid-black' (⬛), 'solid-white' (⬜), or 'solid-square' (◼). That is why 🅱️ travels especially well on partner blood-type-marker markers, blood-type-marker reveals, and any context where the sender wants the message to land with blood energy.
